standard_prerequisites.name: The maximal ideals of the completion contain the extended ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-radical-completion, invoked at proof line 4368
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the extended ideal is contained in the maximal ideal chosen below, which is what yields the conclusion.

core_obligations: Observe that the module is a module over the completion, so the tensor product is too, and choose an element whose annihilator is the given associated prime (proof lines 4357-4361).
Since the element is nonzero, its annihilator in the completion is proper, hence the extension of the prime in the completion is proper and is contained in some maximal ideal (proof lines 4362-4366).
Conclude that the extended ideal is contained in that maximal ideal, so the sum of the prime with the extended ideal is proper (proof lines 4367-4369).
proof_roadmap: Completion module structure and choice of element (proof lines 4357-4361).
Properness of the extended prime and choice of maximal ideal (proof lines 4362-4366).
Containment of the extended ideal (proof lines 4367-4369).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for an adically complete module the associated primes of a tensor product with an arbitrary module never generate the unit ideal together with the extended ideal (statement lines 4348-4355, tag 05JC-adjacent). The proof views everything over the completion, picks an element whose annihilator is the given associated prime, uses that the element is nonzero to find a maximal ideal of the completion containing the extended prime, and concludes because the extended ideal lies in every such maximal ideal. The reduction to the completion is the substance, so the claim is H2.
